title: Introduce invocation resilience index and contextual log coupler
author: Asha Patel
release_notes:
- Add Invocation Resilience Index metric and dashboard
- Ship a log/trace coupling service to attach contextual snippets to sampled traces
- New alerting recipe: resilience-degradation-critical with auto-mitigation playbook
description:
Motivation: Production teams have asked for a single, compact signal that captures invocation-level resilience (successful flow through phases, retries, fallbacks) so SRE and product owners can spot gradual degradation that doesn't surface in percentiles alone. This PR adds an Invocation Resilience Index (IRI) that is computed from phase success flags, retry counts, and fallback activations and exports a decayed-smoothed scalar per invocation. The goal is to provide a low-cardinality, high-signal metric for dashboards and alerting, plus a companion contextual-log coupler that attaches a small, privacy-respecting log excerpt to sampled traces for faster RCA.

What this PR does (summary):
- Introduces the IRI computation in serving/telemetry: telemetry/iri_calculator.go (proto + implementation) and an exporter to metrics pipeline (IRI gauge + histogram for distribution).
- Adds a lightweight trace enrichment microservice (trace-coupler) that joins sampled spans with tenant-permitted log excerpts and injects a compact context blob into traces. The coupler uses existing KMS-tagged retention rules to strip sensitive fields.
- New Grafana dashboard: observability/dashboards/invocation_resilience_index.json (overview, per-route rollup, cohort heatmap).
- Alert tuning: adds an alert rule (slo/resilience_degradation.rule) that uses IRI rolling quantiles and a mute policy for low-volume routes. Includes playbook docs: docs/runbooks/resilience_index_playbook.md.
- Tests: unit tests for IRI weights, end-to-end smoke test that simulates retries/fallbacks and verifies a trace enrichment payload exists for sampled traces.

Notes on implementation details:
- IRI computation is intentionally simple and explainable: a base score from phase successes (input parsing, kv cache lookup, kernel dispatch, response stream) with additive penalties for retries and fallbacks and a multiplicative decay based on invocation age. Weighted config is exposed via telemetry/config and can be adjusted via feature flags.
- The trace coupler subscribes to our sampling bus; when a trace is selected it performs a fast join against a ring-buffered log cache and attaches at most 5 short log lines (sanitized) and a small metadata map (route, model, kernel tag). Coupler runs in the observability namespace and respects per-tenant retention policies (implemented as filter_privacy.go).
- Dashboard shows IRI distribution, delta from baseline, per-route cohort heatmap, and a small panel with coupler-sampled traces (link to trace viewer).

CI / test history: initial CI run reported a flaky e2e failure in iri_smoke_test (random timeout on synthetic runner). Investigated and found the synthetic runner had a race in its goroutine shutdown; fixed in commit "fix: synthetic runner shutdown race". Re-ran CI: all checks passed. Integration harness ran on an isolated cluster (ci/pipelines/iri-integration.yml) and validated end-to-end enrichment at low sample rates. Load bench showed ~0.6% p99 overhead on request path when coupler sampling enabled at 0.1%.

Review conversation (high level):
- Miguel Ortega (comment): "Can you call out how this interacts with existing span sampling? I want to make sure we don't double-sample or leak extra logs for high-volume tenants."
- Asha (reply): "Coupler respects the sampling bus; we do a fast tenant-eligibility check before joining logs. I added a note in filter_privacy.go and the playbook. Also, coupler uses a per-route rate limiter."
- Claire Huang (requested changes): "The dashboard needs clearer labels for the decay window and a toggle for cohort vs route aggregation. Please add panel descriptions and default thresholds in the JSON so PMs understand what's being shown."
- Asha (commit): "docs(dashboard): add panel descriptions + default thresholds" (observability/dashboards/invocation_resilience_index.json)
- Samir Gupta (approval): "Implementation looks good; tests cover weight tuning and the privacy filters suffice for now. Approving after CI green."

Approvals: Miguel Ortega approved (comment + suggestions addressed), Samir Gupta approved, Claire Huang approved after dashboard tweaks.

Merge: squashed and merged into main via squash merge (merge_method: squash). Merge commit message: "Introduce invocation resilience index and trace coupler — adds metric, dashboard, alert, and trace enrichment (A. Patel)"

Operational runbook & follow-ups:
- Runbook (docs/runbooks/resilience_index_playbook.md) includes mitigation steps: temporarily lowering weight of fallback penalty, disabling coupler sampling per-tenant, and an automated throttler runbook.
- Follow-ups filed: ENG-3120 (expose IRI per-model variant in dedicated), ENG-3180 (add ingestion-side aggregation to reduce metric cardinality for per-route histograms).

Risks and mitigations:
- Privacy: coupler strictly enforces retention rules and redaction before attaching logs. We added a short audit log when coupler attaches context to a trace.
- Cost: additional exporter and coupler add CPU; we measured and kept overhead under 1% for default sampling. We will enable gradual rollout by feature flag only for orgs with volume above threshold.

If you want to run locally: see bench/synthetic_resilience_runner/README.md for how to simulate a mix of successful, retry, and fallback invocations and validate the IRI metric series and trace enrichment payloads.

guidance: If the IRI alert fires for a route, reduce fallback_penalty in telemetry/config or disable coupler sampling for that tenant, then assess trace-sampled payloads via the dashboard links.
